by: the quality rules compiled from the smell catalog
check.population: every source file the rules lint
check.freshness: a verdict stands until the linted source or a rule changes
check.refusal: a compiled rule fails the lint stage on the smell's signature
check.observation: none: these records describe decay paths found in source, not signals of a running system
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the smell catalog, which the compiled rules are derived from and the source is held to

records.title: Anti-Pattern Inversion
records.intent: Take any desired architectural principle, invert its invariants, identify the recurring violation shape, model its propagation mechanism, define detection signals, and derive its remediation inverse.
records.invariant: Every anti-pattern is a stable failure algorithm created by repeated violation of an architectural contract.

exemplar.before: Principle: Low Coupling — stated as a goal only; its violations are noticed ad hoc, named inconsistently, and caught late, with no derived failure algorithm.
exemplar.after: Low Coupling → invariant{no bidirectional dependency} → violation{Cyclic Dependency} → propagation{a convenience import closes a cycle, then spreads across modules} → detection{dependency-cycle scan} → remediation{invert the dependency / introduce a port}

records.title: Anti-Pattern Propagation Kernel
records.intent: Start with a local shortcut, repeat it under delivery pressure, normalize it as convention, allow dependent code to form around it, then make remediation expensive through coupling and hidden assumptions.
records.invariant: Most architecture anti-patterns become dangerous when a shortcut becomes infrastructure.

exemplar.before: A one-off shortcut — inline a secret to ship a fix — treated as an isolated, cheap, local choice.
exemplar.after: Shortcut{inline secret} → repetition{reused under deadline} → normalization{becomes the team convention} → dependency-formation{configs read it directly} → institutionalization{deploy scripts assume it} → high-cost-repair{rotate the secret and rewire every dependent}

records.title: Anti-Pattern Remediation Algebra
records.intent: For each anti-pattern, identify the missing architectural control, introduce the inverse control, migrate existing dependents, verify absence of the old failure shape, and enforce recurrence prevention.
records.invariant: Anti-pattern repair is not complete until the propagation path is blocked.

exemplar.before: The anti-pattern is deleted at one call site; the propagation path stays open, so it reappears elsewhere next sprint.
exemplar.after: Secret Sprawl → missing-control{no secret authority} → inverse-control{central store + injected access} → migration{repoint every reader} → absence-check{scan finds zero inline secrets} → prevention-gate{lint rule rejects new inline secrets}

records.title: Architecture Smell Record
records.intent: Model every smell as a recurring degeneration path with trigger conditions, enabling conditions, detection signals, damage model, remediation inverse, and prevention gate.
records.invariant: A smell becomes enforceable when it is represented as a measurable failure contract.

exemplar.before: Smell described in prose ('this class is too big') — unmeasurable, unenforceable, re-argued case by case.
exemplar.after: God Object : trigger{unrelated methods accrete} → degeneration{fan-in/out grows} → detection{LCOM + responsibility count} → measurement{cohesion score below threshold} → remediation{Extract Class} → prevention{architecture test on cohesion}

records.title: Anti-Pattern Rule Compiler
records.intent: Convert each smell record into detection checks, measurable thresholds, severity policy, remediation hints, and recurrence-prevention gates.
records.invariant: A smell catalog is enforced only once it compiles into rules.

exemplar.before: A smell catalog read by the developer — each entry is advice that nothing executes.
exemplar.after: SmellRecord{God Object} → detection-rule{find unrelated method clusters} → metric-threshold{LCOM > 0.7} → severity{error} → refactor-hint{Extract Class} → gate{fails the build}

records.title: Smell Taxonomy
records.intent: Group smells by missing control so detection and remediation can be generalized.
records.invariant: Most bad practices are symptoms of a missing architectural control.

exemplar.before: Dozens of smells listed flat, each handed its own bespoke, unrelated fix.
exemplar.after: smell-set{Magic Value, Secret Sprawl, Hardcoded Path} → missing-control{single source of truth} → rule-family{no-inline-authority checks} → remediation-family{centralize then inject}

records.title: Anti-Pattern Relationship Record
records.intent: Model every anti-pattern as a typed relationship record: name, scope, causal links, conflicts, degradations, enabled failures, detection signals, measurement, remediation inverse, prevention, and severity.
records.invariant: An anti-pattern is enforceable only when it is represented as a typed relationship record.

exemplar.before: An anti-pattern named as free text with no typed edges — not resolvable, not gate-checkable, not linkable to the principle it violates.
exemplar.after: Cyclic Dependency : Anti-Pattern, scope{module}, caused_by{convenience import}, conflicts_with{Low Coupling}, degrades{modularity}, enables_failure{build deadlock}, detected_by{cycle scan}, refactored_by{invert dependency}, prevented_by{dependency rule}, severity{mandatory}

records.title: <Architecture Anti-Pattern>
records.intent: <Local shortcut> → <Missing control> → <Repeated usage> → <Implicit dependency> → <Boundary/contract erosion> → <Systemic fragility> → <Expensive remediation>
records.invariant: Every architecture anti-pattern is a reproducible decay path caused by the absence of a specific control: boundary, contract, ownership, versioning, observability, state isolation, or enforcement.
